catalog_quote: またトーンの體系は H, L, R1, R2 の四つの對立をもつ特徵がある。R に二種類が認められ、後續語の基調が低く設定されるものと高く設定されるものがある。 [...] まだ資料が少ないためか、他の東シンブー諸方言と比較する際にトーンの規則的な對應がうまく見出せない。今後も調査を續けたい。 (p. 179) — sec. 2.4 (p. 163): シンブー諸語はおそらく全てがトーン言語で、語を領域とするメロディーが辨別的であると考へられる。 [...] 東シンブー諸語のトーンは音韻的には語を領域とする對立するメロディーである。メロディーのパタンは高 (high)、下降 (falling)、上昇 (rising)、低 (low)、落調 (key-lowering trigger) の五種類にまとめることができる。 (pp. 163-164) — fn. 3 (p. 164): ノマネ地區の諸方言やグナアについてはトーン對立の在り方がまだ充分に明らかになつたとは言へない。これら方言にはさらに別のメロディー/タイプをトーン音素として認める必要があるが、本稿では扱はない。

new_statements.translation: Also, [the Nomane group] is characterized by a tone system with a four-way contrast H, L, R1, R2. Two kinds of R are recognized: one that sets the register of the following word low and one that sets it high. [...] Perhaps because data are still scarce, regular tone correspondences with the other East Simbu dialects cannot yet be found. — fn. 3: For the dialects of the Nomane area and for Gunaa, it cannot be said that the nature of the tone contrasts has yet been made sufficiently clear; further melodies/types would have to be recognized as tonemes for these dialects, but they are not treated in this paper.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Nomane (Kewa-Meba, Megne/Meine, Kiari varieties) is described as a word-tone language of the East Simbu type: each word carries one of four lexically contrastive melodies (high, low, and two rising tones distinguished by the register they impose on the following word). The source says nothing about stress or accent placement; no stress statement exists in any opened source.
new_statements.exceptions: Author states the Nomane tone inventory is provisional: data are scarce, additional melodies may need to be recognized, and regular correspondences with other East Simbu tones could not be established.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level tone (the paper's general East Simbu characterization is 'melodies whose domain is the word'; longer words tend to carry contour melodies, shorter words level ones). Data from the author's own fieldwork on Kewa-Meba (Digamane) and Megne (Dama) speakers.
new_statements.identity_note: Tida 2011 treats 'Nomane group' as a cluster of varieties spoken in the Nomane (sub-)district: Kewa-Meba, Megne (Meine) and Kiari, described from the author's own fieldwork on Kewa-Meba (Digamane) and Megne (Dama) speakers; this corresponds to Glottolog noma1262 (ISO nof), which has no separate dialect glottocodes. The SIL 2005 wordlists cover the same varieties (Meine/Meiye, Meba, Siarha villages).

sources.quote: またトーンの體系は H, L, R1, R2 の四つの對立をもつ特徵がある。R に二種類が認められ、後續語の基調が低く設定されるものと高く設定されるものがある。 [...] まだ資料が少ないためか、他の東シンブー諸方言と比較する際にトーンの規則的な對應がうまく見出せない。 (p. 179) — fn. 3 (p. 164): ノマネ地區の諸方言やグナアについてはトーン對立の在り方がまだ充分に明らかになつたとは言へない。これら方言にはさらに別のメロディー/タイプをトーン音素として認める必要があるが、本稿では扱はない。
sources.note: Nothing on stress at all; the paper treats East Simbu (incl. Nomane group: Kewa-Meba, Megne/Meine, Kiari) as word-tone languages. Sec. 3.5.1 (p. 179): Nomane group has a four-way word-tone contrast H, L, R1, R2, the two rising tones differing in whether the following word's register is set low or high; fn. 3 (p. 164): the tone contrasts of the Nomane-area dialects are not yet fully clear and further melodies would have to be recognized. General East Simbu remark (p. 165): longer words tend to carry contour melodies, shorter words level melodies.
